scope: Saved-result visual analysis and installed model inspection; no retraining or new benchmark

graphs.name: 01_model_pipeline
graphs.title: Implemented models and information flow
graphs.caption: Conceptual dependency diagram, not measured performance. Speech and document contents are related through derived representations; no jointly trained raw-audio/image fusion network.

graphs.name: 02_fusion_methods_used
graphs.title: Which fusion methods have actually been used?
graphs.caption: The temporal–semantic hybrid combines cues at the score level. It is not an architecture combining early and late neural fusion. Within-text concatenation/ensembling does not create extra input modalities.

graphs.name: 03_controlled_fusion_top1
graphs.title: Controlled fusion diagnostic: semantic-only performs best
graphs.caption: 24 author-designed cases / six constructed slides. Expected NO_CONFIDENT_SLIDE is included in correctness. This is not independent real-meeting accuracy; no claim of universal hybrid superiority.

graphs.name: 04_controlled_fusion_metrics
graphs.title: Fusion quality and coverage measure different things
graphs.caption: Constructed diagnostic only. Macro F1 includes the no-slide class. Hybrid coverage is 100% because it also links unrelated cases; higher coverage is not automatically better.

graphs.name: 05_fusion_case_heatmap
graphs.title: Where each alignment strategy succeeds and fails
graphs.caption: Four cases per constructed group. Timing helps vague references but hurts offscreen/unrelated cases under the fixed 0.5/0.5 score rule and threshold 0.3.

graphs.name: 06_real_unlabelled_coverage
graphs.title: Real example: 39 / 1,008 passages linked; accuracy unknown
graphs.caption: 1008 passages / 34 slides / 0 valid timed slides. Semantic and hybrid agree because of the missing-timing fallback. Independent relevance labels are unavailable; coverage is not accuracy.

graphs.name: 07_discussion_model_vs_baseline
graphs.title: Discussion review: high recall, limited precision
graphs.caption: 11,136 oracle AMI acts, 2,481 positives, 12 meetings / 3 project series; reused historical cohort. Always-negative accuracy is high because of imbalance, but it retrieves no positives. These results do not measure final decisions or raw-audio application accuracy.

graphs.name: 08_discussion_confusion_matrix
graphs.title: Installed discussion classifier: historical confusion counts
graphs.caption: 11,136 human reference dialogue acts: TN 5,627; FP 3,028; FN 467; TP 2,014. Reference text/boundaries differ from deployed ASR passages. Historical cohort was repeatedly inspected.

graphs.name: 09_classifier_family_comparison
graphs.title: Saved discussion classifiers: local versus context features
graphs.caption: Previously examined AMI reference-act cohort. Model-specific development selections differ; this is an exploratory comparison, not independent evidence of ensemble superiority. Installed blend is a separately selected configuration.

graphs.name: 10_speech_wer
graphs.title: Speech models: WER across separate small cohorts
graphs.caption: English development/historical each contain two clips; Hindi and Hinglish each contain eight samples. Missing medium historical bar means unrecorded, not zero. Cohorts are separate; no full-meeting multilingual accuracy claim.

graphs.name: 11_speech_cer
graphs.title: Speech models: CER across separate small cohorts
graphs.caption: English development/historical each contain two clips; Hindi and Hinglish each contain eight samples. Missing medium historical bar means unrecorded, not zero. Cohorts are separate; no full-meeting multilingual accuracy claim.

graphs.name: 12_speaker_threshold_development
graphs.title: Speaker clustering threshold selection
graphs.caption: Small development pilot only; threshold 0.9 was selected before the separate held-out excerpt comparison. This is not a full-corpus calibration curve.

graphs.name: 13_speaker_heldout_der
graphs.title: Diarization: two held-out excerpts and pooled errors
graphs.caption: Two 120-second AMI excerpts; 0.25s collar, overlap included, optimal speaker mapping. Pool by reference speaker-time. Excerpt pilot only; no streaming or physical-device performance claim.

graphs.name: 14_discussion_ensemble_weights
graphs.title: Discussion classifier: 75% forest + 25% logistic
graphs.caption: Installed model configuration, not accuracy or modality importance. Context radius 40 units; smoothing radius 5; threshold 0.35774. These combine text-classifier outputs.

graphs.name: 15_contribution_feature_weights
graphs.title: Default contribution-score weights
graphs.caption: Configuration values, not empirically learned feature importance. Features are max-normalized across participants, then weighted. Missing categories stay zero; the highest participant score need not be one.

graphs.name: 16_gap_participant_rankings
graphs.title: GAP research ranking: outcome alignment, not causal influence
graphs.caption: 28 previously examined meetings / 84 people / 87 comparable pairs. Reference transcripts/speakers, no slides. Ridge research models are separate from the default UI score. Cross-validated exploratory point estimates.

graphs.name: 17_gap_difference_intervals
graphs.title: Ranking differences: descriptive intervals include zero
graphs.caption: Intervals are copied from the saved paired bootstrap, not newly estimated. Previously examined corpus and overlapping CV training sets limit interpretation; no reliable-superiority or fresh-confirmation claim.

graphs.name: 18_gap_feature_coverage
graphs.title: Historical extraction coverage is sparse
graphs.caption: Historical snapshot: 70 / 84 participants and 22 / 28 meetings had no contribution features. No slides were supplied. Later rule fixes were not rerun as a new GAP benchmark.

graphs.name: 19_gap_feature_deletions
graphs.title: Fixed-score deletion diagnostic
graphs.caption: Saved delete-one-feature results on the same historical GAP representation; not retraining or causal feature importance. Inactive features can be removed without changing predictions. No confidence intervals are available.

graphs.name: 20_pipeline_stage_runtime
graphs.title: Stage timing: 90-second English functional recording
graphs.caption: Warm models with uncached meeting inputs; two audio parts, two decks, four-speaker constraint. Excludes upload, queue, decode and final persistence. One laptop run; not a general latency benchmark.

graphs.name: 21_runtime_conditions
graphs.title: Different runtime conditions must remain separate
graphs.caption: Independent panels use different scales and input/cache/resource conditions. These are functional timing records, not a matched comparison of models or cloud hosts. Cached repeat is not fresh inference speed.

graphs.name: 22_ami_discussion_split
graphs.title: AMI discussion subset: meeting split and reference acts
graphs.caption: 47 selected meetings, not the entire AMI corpus. Related series stay together. Historical evaluation contains 12 meetings / three series and was repeatedly examined; act counts are not independent-meeting counts.

graphs.name: 23_gap_role_diagnostic
graphs.title: Historical event-role coverage: a known failure finding
graphs.caption: 8,009 reference utterances. The evaluated historical snapshot emitted no proposals among 537 reference-positive proposal acts. Later keyword fixes do not retroactively update this diagnostic. Roles are not contribution/outcome links.

graphs.name: 24_logistic_feature_coefficients
graphs.title: Installed logistic component: strongest signed coefficients
graphs.caption: Top ten negative and positive coefficients of the actual trusted installed model. Prefix identifies word/character/context feature space. Coefficients depend on correlated TF-IDF features; not causal explanations or full-ensemble probabilities.

graphs.name: 25_forest_feature_importance
graphs.title: Installed random forest: top impurity-based feature importances
graphs.caption: Actual forest component, not permutation importance or causal contribution. Correlated features and impurity-based biases limit interpretation; these importances do not measure the importance of physical input modalities.

graphs.name: 26_discussion_feature_dimensions
graphs.title: Discussion input: concatenated word, character and context features
graphs.caption: Actual feature dimensions supplied to the installed classifiers. Stored unused context variants are excluded. Feature count is not model accuracy or an extra physical modality.

graphs.name: 27_speaker_additional_diagnostics
graphs.title: Speaker pilot: complementary diagnostic measures
graphs.caption: Selected threshold 0.9; only two held-out excerpts. DER/JER and count MAE are lower-is-better; precision/recall/F1 are higher-is-better. Speech detection metrics concern speech activity, not word transcription correctness.

graphs.name: 28_temporal_semantic_fusion_flow
graphs.title: The actual alignment fusion rule and missing-timing fallback
graphs.caption: Configuration/implementation diagram, not measured accuracy. Pure temporal-only and semantic-only settings serve as single-cue baselines. Fixed weighted cue fusion is not learned cross-attention or a neural early-plus-late hybrid architecture.

discussion_metrics.scope: 11,136 oracle AMI acts, 2,481 positives, 12 meetings / 3 project series; reused historical cohort

limitations: Constructed fusion cases are not independent real-meeting accuracy.
Real slide-link coverage is not accuracy; ground-truth relevance labels missing.
Discussion results use historical human text/boundaries, not full ASR application outputs.
GAP is previously inspected outcome-proxy research with reference speakers and no slides.
Historical role/coverage snapshots were not rerun after later extraction fixes.
No matched TF-IDF/MiniLM, learned cross-attention or full end-to-end multimodal accuracy result is claimed.
No ROC/PR curves or uncertainty estimates were fabricated from summary metrics.
